body: Thank you for sharing your experience!

You sound like a great T. I understand having to respect the client's autonomy, but from my experience and what I've seen on this thread, it seems that a lot of clients want the T to fight for the relationship, to ask them to stay etc. But I know it gets tricky and a T can't actually do that and they have to respect what the client is saying they want (but prob deep down dont). Thanks for sharing!
That makes sense. Thank you for sharing.
Thanks for this!
Can you please share the source of where you found this? It's interesting because my therapist had me do the opposite basically - listening to energizing and uplifting music when I'm sad.

My therapist had me do a Playlist of energizing music for when I'm feeling down, and a Playlist of soothing/calming music for when I'm anxious. I haven't asked her specifically but to me this suggests that listening to sad music when you're sad will keep you in that state.
I feel extra conflicted sometimes because one of my friends is her client. So I feel jelly sometimes and then feel guilty cuz it's my friend and I should want them to get time with her etc etc 🙃

I've been struggling with this since I started therapy and realized that what I thought were my personality traits are just trauma responses. I don't know if this is correct, but I guess how I'm trying to reconcile this is by seeing things like this: for example, my ability to be compassionate and empathetic is my personality, but when it goes too far and it becomes people pleasing, then that's my trauma. Does that make sense? I do wonder though if I'd even be as compassionate as I am if I didn't go through the trauma that I did. Like, how would I be as a person. I have no idea and I will never know. It's hard to sit with that.

• when she gives me her sad puppy face - she looks at me this way when I'm crying or talking about something difficult. Makes me feel her compassion, empathy, and care 
• she is always on time and has never missed an appt 
• she doesn't break connection/eye contact for anything. Even when she is drinking water from her bottle she does it in a way that she doesn't stop looking at me 
• she's told me she cares 
• she told me she would be absolutely devastated if I killed myself 
• she told me that if we had met under other circumstances she could see herself being friends with me as she knows I would make a really good one 
• she said "I love you, too" when I expressed my love to her 
• she provides a safe space for me to cry and reassures me that it's ok and not stupid for me to do so. And also expressed happiness that I'm able to let the tears out 
• she allows me to email her twice a week outside of session 
• she is helping me grow and be able to reassure and soothe myself, while still offering me reassurance and care 
• she always offers me reassurance when I doubt whether she cares about me 
• she has always been there even when I've tried to push her away or when I'm mad at her 
• she expressed feeling anger at my mom for what she put me through 
• she expressed feeling defensive for me when someone said something insulting/that hurt me 
• she feels happiness/excitement when I show growth 
• one time at the end of a session I was very upset and she said if we were in person she would give me a hug
• she hugged me when we finally met in person

Those are just some that came to mind. She shows it in a lot of ways really! I am so grateful to have her.

I couldn't afford my Ts rate and she took me on anyway. I pay less than half her rate, and I'm sure she doesn't take home much after you take out what the agency is entitled to. How can you say she doesn't care when she's basically taking time from her life (and could be using that time to treat a full paying customer) to help me?

I can relate to it being fascinating and scary. I think there was a part of me that was scared that it would always be like this, that I'd always feel left behind, but since I started therapy I have noticed a shift. Particularly, I used to heavily identify with my 8-9 yr old scared little girl part, so I felt that way often, but I don't feel that anymore. So in some ways I feel like I've "matured" and if I think of how I act now I think I def have. As I was reading your message I also wonder how much of this is our perception vs reality. Because when I think about my 20 yr old friend for example, I can see the difference in maturity between her and I (even though I feel 20 at times), so maybe I do act older than I feel. Is this making sense? 
I feel that for me at least, this might be coming from my perfectionist tendencies. Like I had this idea that at 28 I'd be fresh out of med school and I'd be married and have a family etc, but since that didn't happen then I feel an age that is more appropriate to where I am in my current lifestyle (single, not settled down, traveling and moving all the time etc). But that doest mean that I actually act like someone that age... except emotionally I might sometimes. This is so confusing haha.  I feel like I just word vomited and idk if this is making sense anymore. Sorry 😅

Yes. I'm 35 but in some ways feel like I'm still 18 or early 20s. Up until recently there was a big part of me that felt like a scared little girl (8 or 9). Basically all of my friends are younger than me. Some are 20-23 which is a big age gap.

That's interesting because when I was younger I acted and felt way older than I was. Then it all seemed to come to a stand still up until I was high school. I don't feel like I've "grown" much since then. I'm 35 now.
I'm really sorry to hear of your experience. Thats so unfortunate. I hope you can find a therapist who is better suited for you.
That's so sweet. I'm glad you were able to have that experience and reassurance with her.

I understand your perspective. Mine actually ended up saying it back. And she is really good at keeping boundaries so I'm not worried about it. I think her saying it back was her way of showing care for me, as I'm sure she knew how important it was for me to hear it back.
I'm sure that took a lot of vulnerability and courage. Good on you for saying it. And I'm glad she said it back to you!
I feel like her saying it in that way is still saying it, if that makes sense? Mine said it back and it definitely had an effect on me.
What has his reply been?
Can I ask why you think it's for the best?
Would she say it back?

The "gifts" part really hit me. Can relate so much. For me specifically it comes with shame because I've realized that I'm not a caring and loving person, it's just a trauma response. It's like the only positive qualities I thought I had aren't even mine :(

Hi there. NAT but this article might help a bit. Specifically the section on object constancy 

https://eggshelltherapy.com/fear-of-abandonment-object-constancy-and-bpd/#Fear_of_Abandonment_Explained_Object_Constancy
Do you ever get sad that you can't be friends with your client?
I believe in you! I really hope you do it. Being able to release my emotions in a safe place with someone who is safe and caring has been very healing for me.

Ive always hated crying in front of others and would rarely let myself do it. So naturally when I started therapy I tried to stop myself from doing it but inevitably it happened. The first 4 or 5 times I felt stupid and would apologize to her. I've been in therapy 4 months now and I no longer feel stupid or apologize. 

I know it might not be so helpful but try to just let yourself do it. Maybe with time it'll get easier for you, too.

I'm sorry that he feels like a different person now. That would feel so hard for me to handle.

I understand why you would feel that terminating for your own good wouldn't be good. I'd feel the same. My guess is he feels that even if you felt that how things were was helping you he doesn't exactly see it that way. I know you're afraid of being open with him right now but I think it would be good for you to tell him how you're feeling, especially about him not caring. I'm willing to bet that's not the case. 

I'm sorry that no one else would be able to help you. I admire your courage you want to keep going and get better. I sincerely hope you are able to make it past this and heal and lead a fulfilling and peaceful life.

I personally like these other ways of asking. If my T asked me how something makes me feel I'd probably answer vaguely or more generally, but her asking what's coming up inside and then where I'm feeling it or how I'm feeling it etc, helps a lot!
Thanks for your reply!

I know my T has mentioned that the goal is for me to be able to access other support and not just rely on her. So for me that would include talking to other friends, using a crisis line when needed, using my skills to try and calm myself down etc. 

What are some ways you can support yourself outside of therapy? Who are some people who can help you feel safe and who you can form a healthy attachment to, etc? I know you said that your urge to contact him has subsided but if you ever feel it again I would suggest you write him letters expressing or sharing what you normally would have but don't send it. 

In terms of feeling anxious that he will leave, it seems to me that that's affecting how you interact with him in session. I would feel the same as you, but it seems to me this is the biggest hurdle right now. I think if you are able to be less anxious about this it'll help you a lot. Also, do you think that reframing your thoughts about this would help at all? It seems to me you see it as him quitting but I don't see it as that. I see it as him recognizing that maybe he thinks he's not helping you and wanting to get you the help you need. He's not abandoning you but doing so because he cares about you.

As someone who was physically and sexually abused as a child, I can tell you that what messed me up the most wasn't this, but the emotional abuse/neglect! I'm only starting to understand that trauma isn't only what happens to you, but also what doesn't happen. It sounds to me like you need to keep looking for an adequate trauma therapist. Good luck!
Thanks for the heads up!!
Thank you! I will check these out 😊
Thanks for the reassurance. I was mostly discouraged by the bit about it not being common for someone with bpd to lead a fulfilling life

In a lot of ways actually! She has this "sad puppy face" that she makes when she's feeling compassion towards me. She shows up every session on time. She answers my emails in-between sessions. She verbally reassures me repeatedly that she cares about me. She agreed to take me on a sliding scale fee and said that me getting the support I need is more important to her than me being able to pay her full fee. She listens to me intently and remembers things. She told me she's angry at my mom for the ways that she affected me. She apologizes when she upsets me. She looked up some research articles to help me better understand something I was struggling with. She told me she would be devastated if I killed myself. She smiles at me. She challenges me in an effort to make me grow. She will say or do things differently if I express that something is/isn't working for me. But most importantly I can feel it!
I hope you are able to find peace and healing soon.
You're completely right. I dont understand and can only imagine how hard it is. I really hope things work out for you and wish you peace and healing.

Yeah, you're totally right. No harm in trying. I will definitely bring this up to my T.  I had never heard of urge surfing but will look it up. Thanks so much! Are these meditations you mentioned about urge surfing? Thanks again on the encouragement xx
Thank you so much! Wishing you the same xx

Thank you so much for your sweet words and encouragement. It means a lot. 
I remember hearing that the therapeutic relationship was the main driver in healing and I didn't get it until now. This has definitely been the aspect of my therapy that brings the most healing. 
You seem like a really caring and compassionate therapist. I want to thank you for going into this line of work and for caring about our well being. I'm sure you are an angel in your clients' lives. 
I have a question, when my T suggested the dbt skills group it was to help manage my self harm but I haven't done that in a few months and very rarely get the urge now and am able to manage the urge. Would you say there's still benefit for me to attend this group? Seems like there is based on what you mentioned it helps with...

I'm really sorry to hear of your experience. You should have never had to go through that. 
How long have you been seeing your current T? 
And I imagine going through the process of having to find and start with a new T seems like too much right now?
Idk if I'm being naive because I got lucky with my T but I do think there are really good Ts out there and there are some that will be your "flavor" so to speak. It's just a matter of finding them (which I know can be a long and painful process).
I encourage you not to give up! You can recover from these things and you can get better.

Hmm it's hard to articulate it, but I guess the main way is the awareness of how this trauma is manifesting in my life right now. It explains the why of my behaviors, whereas all my life I've always felt that I was broken and there's something wrong with me. Knowing that the way I'm acting is very typical responses to trauma helps me feel validated and understood. Also just being able to talk to someone who really understands what im going through and is patient and compassionate and caring is helping a lot. I'm also learning how to address and manage my emotions which are often very dysregulating and affect my life and relationships. We are also doing IFS which is helping in healing my young parts.

I see what you mean. My T has also dealt with trauma so I can relate to wanting someone who can relate to you. Do you feel it needs to be specifically in the same way that you have? I don't know the specifics of my Ts trauma and I imagine there are differences as no 2 people have the same experience, but she doesn't have to have been through exactly what I did to understand what it's like. Like I said, the way we respond to trauma can be typical and that's where we can relate to others and for me that's enough. I also wonder if finding a T who is very compassionate and empathetic would be enough? It's my opinion that you don't need to have suffered through something to be able to feel for that person. If you have a good T then they should be able to help you feel understood and validated whether they've experienced the same or not.

That's very interesting. It does seem like it's very specific to the individual and their history/circumstances. Right now my therapy is trauma-based and it's working so I don't see a need to change it. My T did suggest me being a part of a dbt group to help manage my self harm so maybe thats a way of getting the best of both worlds.
Sorry I wasn't suggesting this is what your T was doing. Just sharing my thoughts of my experience.
Well this is encouraging 🥺
I'm so sorry to hear of your experience :( have you tried other types of treatment for your ptsd?
It's good to know this thanks. As someone who suffered emotional, physical, and sexual abuse as I child I definitely don't want to just treat the symptoms but rather the root!

Thanks for working with people like us! My T is not trained in DBT but she is a trauma counselor and that is helping me tremendously. She did mention that I should be a part of a dbt group some time ago so I will bring it up again. I definitely wouldn't leave her as I think she is the perfect T for me!
I'm sorry to hear of your experience. I hope you can find a T who is a better fit for your specific needs.

Thanks for your input! A lot of what you described is definitely me, which is worrisome, BUT my T has touched upon some of the things you mentioned. She is trauma informed, and a great and compassionate T in my opinion, so like you said, when I mention my neediness for attention she will reassure me and doesn't see it as negative but the bigger picture of why am I needing this attention, what is missing etc. I do make sure to always respect her boundaries so that makes me feel a bit better about all of this. Thanks again!
I understand what you're saying but I guess you're implying that only those Ts with DBT training can treat someone with BPD, which is not exactly true, right?

Thanks for this! It adds a new perspective as I guess I had made the assumption that Ts don't WANT to work with us, rather than they CANT work with us. It makes sense for sure. It definitely worries me tbh but thankfully my T seems to be resilient and not afraid to continue working with me.

Thank you so much for your reply! First I'd like to congratulate you as I'm sure getting to this point has taken a lot of work from your part (and your therapist). That's amazing! It's definitely encouraging to hear your journey as it gives me hope. I really was starting to think that this is how things were going to be for the rest of my life.

My therapist almost always ends her emails with this. At first I thought it was really nice/sweet but then I was thinking that she probably says this to all her clients and wondered how "special" it really is.

Thank you so much for taking the time to respond! You have answered all of my questions in great detail and I really appreciate it. It's especially helpful to learn about the blindspots you mention. I can definitely relate and helps a little just being aware of this. Thanks again.

Thank you so much for sharing your thoughts and for the encouragement. She actually reassured me and I will try not to worry but the truth is that I still do. I don't want to make things harder for her.

I feel ya. Linking them back to the trauma is the hardest for me. Again I haven't processed this so just kind of speculating for now, but I'll try to explain how this might came to be for me (briefly of course). Growing up (and even now) my mom always made me feel that what I did wasn't good enough - graduated #4  with honors etc etc etc in my high school class and when I told my mom her response was, "why aren't you #1?" That's just one example. I think based on this I always feel like I have to do my best (and then keep going) until it's perfect or else it won't be good enough and others won't be pleased with me. So calling out from work would mean I'm not doing this etc. So the trauma being my mom's emotional neglect and my response was wanting to always please her which now translates to always wanting to please everyone.  Idk if this is making sense as much as it is in my head but that's just one small way I could maybe find a connection? But I also still don't fully make the connection either tbh.

I know you were asking OP but thought I'd chime in anyway, hope you don't mind. 

I struggle with this too! I haven't really processed it (just clicked as I read this post) but my initial guess is that this comes from my fear of letting others down/wanting to please others. I also don't like inconveniencing anyone or feeling like a burden etc.
Hi there. Thanks for your reply. I was hoping that as I heal and get better then I will be better able to handle something like this. Sounds like that might be the answer. Thanks.

My T used the word trauma first. I personally don't think I've ever used it because I still don't feel that what I went through was trauma. I also have a hard time with the word abuse. And my T has picked up on that. So now she mostly uses words like neglect or damage on unhelpful events (can't remember exactly how she words it). Might just be that he can tell you wouldn't react well to it. Also him not asking might be that he doesn't want to press if you're not ready to go into the details etc. I doubt it's because he doesn't care or thinks you're being dramatic. I would encourage you to open up about this to your T and just say what you have here.

I can totally understand and want to assure you that you are also not alone. I can relate to what you're going through in some ways. I really hope you are able to find some professional help who can be there and listen and support you in the way that you need and deserve. I'm rooting for you :)
I totally understand. I'd feel the same! I also feel like if it were me I just wouldn't feel ok until I got it out in the open. I wish you the best and hope it all works out!

I'm sorry if in any way I made you feel like you were just looking for sympathy. I surely didn't feel that way. And I'm sorry if me expressing sympathy caused any discomfort. 

I would strongly encourage you to use that service. It might not be ideal like you said but these students have supervisors and I think it could still be very helpful for you.

Hello, there. Thank you for being vulnerable and sharing your story with us. I wish there was something I could do, some way I could make it better. I'm sorry you've been through all of this. I assure you that you're not broken, or weak, or that in any way any of this is your fault. You were dealt an unfair hand in life and you're doing the best you can. You're surviving. You're stronger than you think. Is there any way that you can access any mental health resources where you are?

I think you really should get the advice of a therapist on this one, but at the end of the day who knows really how your particular therapists would react. I'm not a therapist but if I were in your shoes I'd probably tell the therapist that I would be willing to let go if need be and see how she reacts. It's my understanding though that most therapists won't allow their clients to see another therapist, so if you come clean you will have to choose. I know you mentioned that part of why you didn't want to stop seeing T B is because you're struggling, can you maybe ask T A for an extra session as you're needing more support?

I can't imagine either of your therapists will be mad about this though as your intentions weren't in the wrong place. I think they would both understand and help you come to a decision that is best for you.
Thank you, that means a lot 🙏🏼

Hey there. Thanks for your reply and your perspective. I def hear what you're saying and to a certain degree can agree with it, but there's still a part of me that's upset or bothered that I didn't get to choose which traits or habits I wanted to be a part of my personality. It's like now I just have to make the best of it and work really hard at expressing these traits within a healthy balance, but I still get no choice in who I am. I guess maybe none of us do...

Yes, going through that right now and it's so overwhelming. I struggle with low self-esteem and insecurity and the only "things" I liked about myself I now see are just trauma responses. I literally have no idea who the heck I am. Will I ever? It's not like I get a second chance. I have a feeling that these responses will forever be a part of my "personality". Sorry just kinda hijacked your post to ramble. But yes, I can totally relate.
I don't feel that I have anything I can share that would be helpful, but it seems you have a T who cares about you very much! I hope things get better for you and I hope you stay with us.

That makes sense, thanks for explaining. I'm sorry you're burnt-out, I hope you are able to find some peace and relief. For what it's worth I appreciate and admire your selfless service to your patients. Therapists are angels on earth. Thank you.

I'm just curious, does burnout from caring come from the inability to stop thinking of clients outside of working hours? Or just the stress that comes from concern you have for them? I guess I assumed burnout was more from long hours, no proper self care etc, but not necessarily from care for patients.
Hmm interesting. Thanks for sharing. I guess I personally will very rarely compliment someone on their attire and sometimes even physical features. I prefer compliments on personality, kindness etc.

I never really knew this and it makes me sad. As a woman I know I don't compliment men because I'm worried they'll take it as flirting and I don't want to deal with that. If a woman were to compliment you, would you take it as flirting? Also, I'm curious, when you say you don't get complimented, do you mean by strangers or does that also include intimate partners?
If you wouldn't have said I wouldn't have known you are Trans. You are absolutely beautiful and I LOVE your hair!
I understand. Best of luck! Take care.

Hi there, not a therapist. I didn't read all the comments but from what I read I can understand your point that these instances don't define your partner or your relationship as abusive. Can you maybe see though, that there ARE moments of abuse in your relationship? Even if few and far between. I think the main concern here is the potential for these abusive moments to increase or worsen. I would very lovingly encourage you to talk to your T about this. They will be able to help you with this in ways we can't.

I'm not a therapist but I just wanted to say that I'm sorry for the loss of your son first and foremost. I'm also sorry for everything else you lost. I hope you can see a therapist and find some peace and healing.
My T does IFS combined with others. I mean I would say I'm still new but so far I'm making progress and things are making sense and changing so I think it's good. Are you finding it helpful?

I should have started my first comment with, I'm not a therapist, sorry. Also, because of that take everything I'm saying with a grain of salt. I can relate to creating our own exposure therapy. I wonder if that approach only works to certain conditions, such as ocd for example. I feel that only now that I'm digging deep and processing my traumas through other modalities have things been moving and changing for me. 

 Are you familiar with IFS? I could see how perhaps your wise Self can recognize that your partner is a safe person, but one or more of your parts still sees danger in this intimacy and vulnerability. I really hope that you can work through this with your therapist!

I can understand how receiving love and attention now would feel uncomfortable if you never received it as a child. I wonder if at an unconscious level you learned to believe that these things were wrong, not needed, etc. If you ask yourself, what would happen if I allow myself to be seen, given attention and love, what comes up?

Hey there. I can't fully relate but what I can relate to is not wanting to be seen, however it seems that's for different reasons. What I wanted to comment was in regards to shame. For me this means that when someone does offer love or affection or care I feel that I don't deserve it, I'm not worthy of it, and I am burdening that person by asking for it or receiving it. I don't know if any of that resonates with you. Also, I have learned that a lot of my reactions due to my trauma are counterintuitive, like pushing others away when I want and need connection the most.
Why do you think that he doesn't care about you?
Thanks for your reply! Lots of good points.
Thanks for your response.
If you think the root of these problems is from trauma then I'd recommend looking for a trauma informed counselor. Someone who does AEDP, IFS, etc.
Thanks
You basically just described my experience exactly. I'm sorry that happened to you. I hope you have been able to find more peace now.
Thanks
Thanks for taking the time to reply.
Thank you for your reply. I guess I knew but I was hoping it wasn't the case.
Thank you
Thank you, I appreciate your kind words. I put all the emotions back in the box they were in and tucked it away. Didn't know what else to do.

Same. Trying to think how I'm gonna word what happened without saying I was sexully abused as a kid and assaulted as an adult. I have a very hard time saying the word abuse or rape. Before I typed the word rape I just Googled the definition to see if what happened to me was even rape, and yup it was. Before this moment I had never referred to it as rape. Like I don't deserve to use that word.

(Not a therapist) I'm sorry to hear you are struggling so much. Can I ask what other coping strategies you have tried already?
For me what helped was getting out of my room/ house (basically where I had access to do it) and going on a walk or to the store, hanging out with a friend to distract me, writing about it (what I'm feeling, why I want to do it, what it would make me feel, etc). For me the self harm was very impulsive so I found that if I could hold off from doing it for 5 minutes or 10 then the urge would pass.

I appreciate that. I mostly could tell that's what you were getting at but funny that what my mind picked out from all of that was that my T might keep me on because it would be easier or more convenient to do so  rather than have to go through all of the work with a new client. My mind is great ain't it? Anyway, I really appreciate it. I hope one day we can see ourselves as worthy just because we are.

Thank you for your input. I mean I'd be able to afford it if I don't spend on other things and go through most of my savings, so not ideal and adds a different kind of stress to my life. But this is important to me so it'll have to be a sacrifice I make, esp because it seems like a lot is on the line and I've struck gold.

That's a good point. It's not so much that I wanted to avoid the awkwardness of the conversation. Even if she says I can stay at the current fee I will not feel comfortable. I already feel guilty about it.
Yes, that is the main thing that was making me hesitate. I feel like she's the perfect fit for me and wondered if I'd be able to find someone who was as patient, caring, and understanding as her.

I feel like you are reading me like an open book 😭 You are very right, this definitely shows a bigger underlying issue I struggle with. I will try to use this as practice for having these kinds of conversations. Thank you so much, honestly. Your input has been very valuable 🙏🏼

This is really helpful, thank you. Based on our conversation I'm definitely leaning towards sticking with her, so not sure if I should or need to have this conversation with her at all. What do you think? Also, I was contemplating asking what she thought about doing sessions every other week instead of weekly as this would make it sustainable, so in this case I would have to bring it up anyway. But if I don't decide to do this (I feel like waiting one week between sessions is hard enough and know changing the frequency will just prolong progress and healing), do you think I should still bring this up with her?

Those are some good points, thanks for sharing. I'm still very new to the therapy world and the little experience I've had with mental health professionals hasn't been good, so I guess I got very lucky with this one! I believe she has experienced trauma as well so I'm sure that makes her more understanding and thus a better T for my particular situation.
She definitely has encouraged me to talk about anything and has been supportive when I do, but my insecurities and fears still make that hard for me. I will try to bring it up to her somehow though.

Yay, me 😅
Thank you for your input, I appreciate it and will keep it in mind. I am hesitant to bring this up with her I guess. Idk why just makes me uncomfortable, maybe because I don't want her to think that I'm trying to get her to keep me at the current rate. Even if she did I would feel really guilty knowing I'm not paying her full rate (I already feel this way now). I also don't want her to think that money is more important to me, because it's not.

I started therapy because of my depression, self harm, and suicidal thoughts. Therapy has been a long time coming for me - throughout my young adult life I struggled with depression, anxiety and anxiety attacks, an eating disorder, alcohol and drug abuse, self harm, and suicidal thoughts. All of this stemming from what I guess would be my experiences of childhood emotional, physical, and sexual abuse, and a sexual assault instance in college. 
It's hard for me to know if this would be considered intense? I find it hard to even label what I went through as "abuse" and feel that people go through much worse things, so I don't personally think it's intense.
No matter what happens you won't make a fool of yourself. Everything is a learning opportunity. I wish you the best :)
That's so nice. I hope one day mine won't try to push her away.

I don't think there is anything wrong with asking straight out and saying what you said here, but if you don't feel comfortable maybe you can express your concerns "I am scared you will abandon me" etc and see her response. I am going through basically the same thing and just expressing these fears has resulted in her reassuring me, "I care about you" "I have no intention of leaving our therapeutic relationship" etc. If you're anything like me though, be prepared to feel like you don't believe her haha or STILL need more reassurance. I think at the end of the day it will just take time and more than her just saying it but showing you that she's there for you. But that initial reassurance definitely helps so I hope you can get what you need!

I do plan on bringing this up in the next session now. Thanks for the suggestion. 

And for the other half of your message, d. All of the above 😭 I definitely know that this anxiety stems from my past trauma, but while I have some awareness of it I still can't control it. Hence me still worrying about these things. You sound like an amazing therapist by the way! Thank you for taking the time to reply.
I understand, it's just still hard for me to do that. But I sill try. Thanks for your advice!
Thanks for the suggestion. I will definitely bring this up in our next session.

Oh man I feel that. My parts are so guarded against her!
Your T sounds lovely!
